name: Qaiyo Timeline Events
author: qaiyo

sections.description:
Qaiyo Timeline Events displays a beautiful program timeline — perfect for conferences, webinars, meetups, workshops, product launches and company milestones.

One event, all its time slots

You create an event — the whole conference, workshop day or launch — and add its time slots inside it, in one screen. Drag them into order, open a slot to fill in its details, and everything saves as you type. Layout, colors and display options belong to the event, so the same program can look completely different from one event to the next.

Duplicate an event

“Duplicate” in the events list (or “Copy to a new draft” in the editor) copies an event with all of its time slots, settings, details and password into a new draft — next year’s conference or a second workshop day is ready in seconds.

Finished time slots fade by themselves

Time slots that have ended are dimmed and labelled “Ended”, and the carousel opens at the next one. It happens in the visitor’s browser and repeats every minute, so it stays right on cached pages too. Switch it off per event, or per page with dim_past="0".

When and where

Give a time slot an end time, a location and an online link. The card shows the time range, the place and a “Join online” link; “Add to calendar” and the .ics download take the real end, the location and the link along, and search engines learn whether a session is on site, online or both.

Not only events: process timelines

Set an event’s “Timeline type” to “Process (steps)” for a how-it-works or step-by-step timeline. Its steps are not events, so the cards carry no schema.org Event markup, there are no calendar buttons and no “Ended” label, and search engines get an ordered ItemList of the steps instead of an EventSeries. Steps have no time or date: the editor hides those fields and the cards show none. Override it per page with mode="process" or mode="event".

Layouts

  • Vertical timeline — a classic agenda with a time rail, animated cards and colored dots.
  • Horizontal carousel — an elegant, swipeable card carousel with arrows, dots, keyboard navigation and optional autoplay.

Shortcode and Gutenberg block

  • A block editor block with a live preview and an event picker — no shortcode needed.
  • The classic [qaiyo_timeline_events] shortcode for any page builder or widget.

Add to calendar

  • Per-event “Add to calendar” buttons: Google Calendar and a downloadable .ics file.
  • A one-click .ics export of the whole program, ready to import into any calendar app.

Design that matches your site

  • The accent color is detected automatically from your theme or page builder — Elementor, Bricks Builder, Divi, Oxygen and Gutenberg (theme.json) are supported.
  • Heading and body fonts follow the theme’s global typography (Elementor, Bricks).
  • Dark and light color schemes.
  • Per-event accent color, badge (label + icon + colors), card padding, title size and timeline rail (solid or dashed, width, light and dark color).
  • Individual time slots can override the accent color and badge when one of them needs to stand out.

Speaker cards

  • Speaker name, company, and photo from the Media Library (circular crop) — or an automatically generated monogram avatar.
  • Optional moderator row above the timeline.

SEO / AEO ready

  • schema.org Event microdata on every card.
  • An EventSeries JSON-LD block for search engines and AI assistants.
  • You control the title HTML tag (p, h3–h6, span) — never an extra H1.

Accessible (WCAG 2.2 AA)

  • The carousel follows the WAI-ARIA carousel pattern: a Stop/Start button whenever it rotates on its own, rotation pauses on hover and keyboard focus, slides out of view are taken out of the tab order, and slide changes are announced.
  • Arrow, dot and calendar buttons have accessible names and a visible focus ring; every target is at least 24 × 24 px.
  • Text drawn in your accent color is darkened or lightened automatically until it reaches 4.5:1 contrast, so a pale theme color never produces unreadable labels.
  • Reduced-motion and Windows high-contrast (forced colors) modes are respected.
  • In the editor every field has a label, and time slots can be reordered with Move up / Move down buttons as well as by dragging.

Works with any theme

  • Sizes are set in pixels, not rem, so a theme that changes the root font size cannot shrink the timeline; theme styles for links, buttons and headings are reset inside the timeline.

Multilingual

  • Fully translatable, including the block editor — translations are delivered through translate.wordpress.org, and the plugin ships a .pot template.
  • Polylang and WPML compatible (wpml-config.xml included); works with TranslatePress and Loco Translate.

Dashboard

  • With Qaiyo Admin Booster active, the Qaiyo dashboard widget shows a Timeline Events card: the time slot on right now, the next three upcoming ones linked to their event, and how many events and time slots you have. Nothing is added to the dashboard otherwise.

Usage

Create an event under Timeline Events, add its time slots, then add the block or copy the shortcode shown right in the event editor:

[qaiyo_timeline_events id="123"]

Everything else is optional — the attributes below override the event’s own settings for one placement:

Attributes: id (the event), title, subtitle, badge, moderator, mod_role, date (program day, for calendar export), theme (dark/light), layout (vertical/horizontal), orderby (auto/time_asc/time_desc/date_asc/date_desc), autoplay (ms), max, dim_past (1/0), mode (event/process).

Qaiyo Timeline Events Pro adds multi-day and multi-track agendas, an alternating steps layout, highlight notes, a live “happening now” mode with a countdown, reusable speaker profiles, front-end filtering and CSV import/export.

External services

This plugin relies on the following external services. No data is sent anywhere unless one of the situations below applies.

1. WordPress.org plugin directory API (api.wordpress.org)

Used only on the admin screen “Discover Qaiyo”, to list this author’s free plugins available on WordPress.org. The request is made by your site when a logged-in administrator opens that screen, and the result is cached for 12 hours. It sends no personal data and no information about your site — only the query for the plugin list. This is WordPress’s own infrastructure.
Privacy: https://wordpress.org/about/privacy/

2. Google Calendar (calendar.google.com)

The “Add to calendar → Google” button is a plain link. Nothing is sent while the page loads. Only when a visitor clicks it does their browser open Google Calendar, passing the event title, description and start/end time in the link, along with the visitor’s IP address and user agent as with any website visit. Visitors who never click the button send nothing to Google. The .ics download is generated by your own site and involves no third party.
Terms: https://policies.google.com/terms — Privacy: https://policies.google.com/privacy
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin to /wp-content/plugins/ or install it from the Plugins screen.
  2. Activate it.
  3. Create an event under Timeline Events, add its time slots, then place the block or the [qaiyo_timeline_events] shortcode on a page.
sections.faq:
Does it delete my events when I uninstall the plugin?

No. By default all events, their time slots and settings are kept, so reinstalling restores everything. You can opt into full data removal under Timeline Events → Settings → Data & maintenance.

Can I sort the time slots manually?

Yes — drag them into place in the event editor. That order is what the timeline uses by default; you can switch to sorting by time or date under the event’s Display settings.

Which page builders are supported for color/font detection?

Elementor, Bricks Builder, Divi, Oxygen and Gutenberg (theme.json). Without any of them, a neutral blue accent is used — and you can set a custom accent on each event.

I used the old “Event Timeline” plugin. Will my events survive?

Yes. Each of your old event groups becomes an event, and the entries in it become its time slots — nothing is deleted and no content is rewritten. Existing group="…" shortcodes keep working, and the event editor shows you the new id="…" shortcode to switch to when you are ready.

Can visitors see draft or private events?

No. The timeline, its calendar downloads and every add-on endpoint only show an event that is published and not password-protected — or one the logged-in user may read in the admin.

How do the “Add to calendar” buttons work?

Each time slot with a date gets a Google Calendar link and a downloadable .ics file, and the whole program can be exported as a single .ics. If your time slots only carry a time (no date), set the event day in the event’s Display settings so the calendar entries know when they happen. You can turn the buttons off under Settings → Add to calendar.
sections.changelog:
1.2.0

  • New: end time, location and online link on every time slot. The cards show the time range (“10:00 – 11:30”), the place and a “Join online” link; the calendar buttons and the .ics file carry the real end, the location and the link; the “Ended” mark waits for the real end; search engines get endDate, location (a place, a virtual location or both) and the attendance mode. A process has none of them.
  • New: “Background: Transparent” in the event’s Display settings leaves out the timeline’s own box (and its padding), so it sits on your page’s background — in the light and the dark theme. background="none" / background="solid" shortcode attribute; the block has it too, along with a switch to hide the event title.
  • New: heading="0" shortcode attribute hides the timeline’s own title on a page that has its own heading; the title still names the timeline for screen readers and search engines.
  • Time slot editor: the color fields have a color picker beside them, and the per-slot overrides are always visible.
  • New: “Duplicate” on every time slot copies it with all of its fields right below the original.
  • The live preview follows the chosen layout (add-on layouts too), shows the first three time slots and updates while you type, add, duplicate, reorder or delete slots.
  • A process has no time or date: the time slot list hides the Time column and the Date field, and the cards print neither.
  • Developers: Qaiyo_Timeline_Events_Shortcode::for_display() (row meta as a card shows it); the time slot list carries the chosen layout (data-qte-layout) and the editor fires qaiytiev:layout, so an add-on can show a slot field only for its own layouts; the live preview hands add-ons the slots and a card builder (qaiytiev:preview).

1.1.1

  • New: “Timeline type” in the event’s Display settings. “Process (steps)” is for a how-it-works or step-by-step timeline: no schema.org Event markup on the cards, no calendar buttons, no “Ended” label, and an ordered ItemList in the JSON-LD instead of an EventSeries. mode shortcode attribute. The date-only settings (Event day, dimming) are hidden for a process, and a process never appears among the upcoming slots of the Admin Booster card.
  • Developers: Qaiyo_Timeline_Events_Shortcode::is_process(), ::label(), ::print_item_scope() and ::print_start_date() for add-on layouts.

1.1.0

  • New: duplicate an event with all of its time slots (“Duplicate” in the events list, “Copy to a new draft” in the editor); a password-protected event stays protected in the copy. Developers: qaiyo_timeline_events_duplicated action, qaiyo_timeline_events_duplicate_skip_meta filter.
  • New: finished time slots are dimmed and labelled “Ended” (in the browser, every minute — cache-safe), and the carousel opens at the next slot. Per-event setting, dim_past shortcode attribute.
  • New: with Qaiyo Admin Booster, a Timeline Events card in the Qaiyo dashboard widget — the slot on right now, the next three and the totals.
  • New: the admin menu joins the Qaiyo plugin group when another Qaiyo plugin draws it; this plugin never restyles the admin menu itself.
  • New: Qaiyo_Timeline_Events_Shortcode::output() prints a timeline for page builders; qaiyoTimelineEvents.carousel() / .past() re-run the front-end scripts after a late render.
  • Accessibility: stronger contrast for secondary text, purple text and code on the Settings page; the footer link is underlined; the editor preview uses the front end’s color tokens.
  • Fix: the Settings page background now applies in every admin language.
  • Translations: bundled catalogues load only when no language pack is installed, regional locales use their base language, and the block editor’s strings follow.

1.0.0

  • Initial release.
  • Event-centric editing: one event holds all of its time slots, with drag-and-drop or Move up / Move down ordering and inline autosave.
  • Per-event layout, colors, header and display settings, including a configurable timeline rail (solid or dashed, width, light and dark color).
  • Vertical timeline and horizontal carousel layouts, each with an SVG preview in the layout picker.
  • Gutenberg block with a live preview and event picker, plus the [qaiyo_timeline_events id="…"] shortcode.
  • Add to calendar: per-time-slot Google Calendar links and .ics downloads, and a whole-program .ics export (RFC 5545 line folding, UTF-8 safe).
  • Theme accent color and typography detection (Elementor, Bricks, Divi, Oxygen and block themes via theme.json), skipping near-white and near-black palette entries.
  • Speaker cards with photos or monogram avatars, badges, and per-event styling.
  • schema.org Event microdata and an EventSeries JSON-LD block.
  • Accessibility: WCAG 2.2 AA carousel, automatic contrast for accent-colored text, labelled editor fields, keyboard reordering, reduced-motion and forced-colors support.
  • Security: drafts, private and password-protected events never render, export or answer the add-on endpoints for visitors; every CSS value is allowlisted on save and checked again on output; JSON-LD cannot close its script element; add-on markup and attributes go through allowlists.
  • Every post type, taxonomy, meta key, script handle and JavaScript object carries the plugin’s own prefix; data saved under the older “tle_” names is renamed once, automatically.
  • Deleting an event also deletes its time slots; uninstall can optionally remove every event, time slot and setting (multisite aware), and always clears caches.
  • Fully translatable through translate.wordpress.org, including the block editor; a language pack always takes precedence.
  • Dashboard card for the Qaiyo Admin Booster widget (now, next three, totals); the admin menu joins the Qaiyo plugin group when another Qaiyo plugin draws it — this plugin itself never restyles the admin menu.
  • Extension hooks for add-ons: qaiyo_timeline_events_layouts, _layout_panels, _row_fields, _save_row, _save_program, _program_settings, _shortcode_defaults, _context, _pre_render, _before_timeline, _after_timeline, _after_wrap, _card_bottom, _speaker_html, _card_attributes, _event_meta, _json_ld, _event_duration, _primary_color, _theme_fonts, _settings_defaults, _pro_features, _unlocked_features, _upgrade_url.
